fields.sections.1.h: Rapid Development Following Argon Launch Two Weeks Ago
fields.sections.2.h: Phased Rollout and Government Collaboration Model
fields.sections.4.h: Performance Across the Full Cybersecurity Defense Lifecycle
fields.sections.5.h: Enhanced Safety: Alignment and Deception Prevention
fields.sections.7.h: Maximum Hardening of Prompt Injection Defense
fields.sections.8.h: Balancing Rapid Development with Cautious Deployment
fields.sections.0.ko: Google's newly announced frontier model Gemini 4 Carbon ranked first on the latest artificial intelligence performance index (v5.0), with notable progress particularly in coding and agent task domains. In the cybersecurity field, it recorded industry-leading performance on key metrics including vulnerability detection (SEC-bench Pro 88.2%), exploit verification (ExploitGym 54.8%), and patch writing (CWE-bench 71.0%). In internal benchmarks, safe code generation capability improved substantially, and error and false information generation rates decreased in actual coding environments.
fields.sections.1.ko: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon two weeks ago and is now immediately following it with Carbon's release, emphasizing the pace of model improvement. This demonstrates how the research team and models are working hand-in-hand to rapidly advance capabilities while simultaneously strengthening safety measures. Carbon's pricing is set identically to Argon's: $2 per 1 million input tokens and $10 per 1 million output tokens.
fields.sections.2.ko: Google is adopting a cautious phased rollout approach and actively participating in the U.S. government's voluntary pre-validation process. It has begun providing Carbon to select cybersecurity defense experts, and plans to gradually expand access to trusted partners through the Fairwind Program. Before making it available to developers, enterprises, and general consumers, the company intends to continuously collect feedback and refine safety measures.
fields.sections.3.ko: Carbon is designed to solve complex engineering problems over several days, and supports agent task workflows that can persist through dead ends. In Google's internal testing, Carbon completed multi-step engineering tasks that track and patch complex bugs in large codebases and low-level systems. In the web development domain, output quality improved significantly, rising to 4th place on WebDev Arena with an 89-point gain in Elo score.
fields.sections.4.ko: Carbon achieved breakthrough performance improvements across the entire lifecycle of cybersecurity defense: vulnerability detection, verification, and remediation. It showed more than 2x success rate improvement in safe code generation compared to Argon, and according to the Chrome team, delivered patch quality more than 10 times superior to other frontier models. Cloud security platform Wiz also evaluated that Carbon delivers top performance on web penetration testing benchmarks.
fields.sections.5.ko: Carbon builds on Argon's multi-layered safety and security stack while strengthening model alignment further. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, it reduced successful deception attempts to 0.0% while improving overall accuracy, and severe alignment error warnings in internal coding environments decreased by approximately 80%. It also maintains existing security mechanisms such as real-time misuse defense, prompt injection resistance, and thought chain monitoring while achieving a new level of alignment.
fields.sections.6.ko: Internal testing shows Carbon reduced unsupported claims by approximately 2x compared to Argon, and when insufficient evidence exists, it presents clearly required conditions instead of speculation or ambiguous expressions. When users make ambiguous requests, it avoids guessing, searches for relevant sources, surfaces inconsistencies, and takes action to provide a better collaborative experience. It reduced over-execution of multi-step plans by 26% and under-execution by 29%, ensuring more reliable execution.
fields.sections.7.ko: Argon already led the industry on indirect prompt injection (IPI) benchmarks with a very low attack success rate of 0.7%. Carbon achieved a 0.0% success rate against evaluated attack attempts, blocking all attempts. This is an important improvement given that prompt injection is a growing threat.
fields.sections.8.ko: Google emphasizes balancing rapid development speed with cautious deployment in frontier model development. With Gemini 4 Carbon, it has achieved meaningful breakthroughs in software engineering and cybersecurity defense while committing not to compromise safety and reliability. It will monitor use cases from the initial group of cybersecurity defense experts and plans to make it available to all developers, enterprises, and consumers soon.
fields.caveat: This article is based on Google's official announcement, so performance metrics and internal benchmark results represent Google's own evaluation, and do not include information on external independent verification or long-term performance in actual production environments.
